scenes.title: Jack at the Purgatory, Reading Duty Rosters

beats.text: Jack is on shore leave in the Purgatory and reading duty rosters for her students anyway. Shepard can tell her to keep at it or push her to lighten up, and it colours the whole conversation.
Told she has taken to military life, her answer is that their little suicide squad apparently taught her something about teamwork.

If her kids went to the front, she is watching the higher-ups so they are not handed something out of their league, and is openly surprised at how they hold up under fire. If they took support roles, they are spread through Alliance units running barriers and modding ammo and saving a lot of lives.
Where she takes the job seriously, her kids saw action on Palaven — Prangley's biotics against cannibals, Rodriguez not panicking.
By 2186 she has grown her hair out and, in her own summary, become dependable, which she blames on Shepard.

evidence.text: Requires: Complete Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation and choose the Renegade option, sending the students to war. **Military Strength:** 75 By pooling their powers together, these gifted students from Grissom Academy can launch biotic artillery strikes that impact targets with the force of a bomb. The process is taxing, but devastates any enemy's front lines. While they've only had a few months of training, Grissom's students are eager to prove themselves in the war.
evidence.for_key: Grissom students assigned to Alliance support lines

evidence.text: After the rescue from Jon Grissom Academy, Jack can be found on the Citadel in Purgatory Bar after the attempted Cerberus coup reading duty rosters for her kids even while on shore leave. Shepard can either tell her to keep at it, or convince her to lighten up a bit, which colors Jack's responses throughout the conversation. If Shepard thinks Jack fits in snugly to military life, Jack says that their little suicide squad apparently taught her something about teamwork. If the students had been sent to the front lines, Jack mentions her kids are being sent into hot spots for hit\-and\-runs and she's making sure the higher\-ups won't give them something way out of their league. She expresses her surprise at their ability to hold up under fire, but then Shepard believed in the students' abilities and burned away her doubts. If the students had been assigned support roles, she remarks they've been spread out across Alliance units, saving a lot of lives by providing barrier support, modding ammo and the like, and that they're handling the support duties well. If Shepard convinced Jack to take her job seriously, Jack mentions that her kids even saw action on Palaven, either on the front lines with Prangley displaying exceptional biotic aptitude against Cannibals and Rodriguez not panicking for a change, or that her kids provided barriers for a krogan squad so the latter can get close and break enemy lines. They manage to help the turians evac a thousand civilians to safety. Jack suggests fighting would be more fun with Shepard as the Commander finds bigger fights, but claims the "little shits" would be useless without her, and blames Shepard for the perception that she's apparently "dependable" now. If Jack was previously romanced, Shepard has the option to rekindle or officially end their relationship at this time. The Commander asks Jack to dance with them, regardless of whether she was romanced or not, claiming that she's on shore leave and the rosters can wait. Jack flat\-out retorts that everyone knows Shepard can't dance, and with that they both enjoy the music. If Shepard does not help Grissom Academy in time, she will appear as an indoctrinated Phantom when Shepard raids Cerberus Headquarters. An audio log can be found where Jack is heard resisting her captors up until the end. After the squad is forced to kill her, Shepard states that she was no longer herself and that she is "just one more thing Cerberus will answer for." In the final battle on Earth, Shepard can speak with the communications officer in order to call Jack. Jack indicates that she's in the fight but can't reach Shepard's location. If a male Shepard has a romance with Jack, Jack will tell Shepard that he needs to survive, because she is "getting laid" after the war is over. If Shepard chooses to use the Crucible, Jack can be seen gazing at the stars in the future. If Jack didn't have a relationship with Shepard by the time the Commander uses the Crucible, her fate will be determined by the path her students took. She will either be seen visiting her students' graves if they were previously sent to the front lines, or she will be seen with her kids — alive — and Kahlee Sanders mulling their next move if the students were relegated to support. If Jack did not survive Shepard's suicide mission or was killed on Cronos Station, her name will be engraved in the memorial wall on the Normandy as Jacqueline Nought, a pseudonym she used at least once in the past.

evidence.page: Getting the Biotic Students Off Grissom Academy
evidence.text: Getting the Biotic Students Off Grissom Academy. 2186, after Priority: Palaven, before Priority: The Citadel II Jon Grissom Academy, Petra Nebula — security office, classrooms, Orion Hall, the Atrium, the docking area; then the Normandy After Priority: Palaven, Samantha Traynor tells Shepard she picked an Academy evac request off Alliance comm channels answered by a turian vessel, and that she and EDI traced the answering signal to Cerberus — the rescue is a fake and the station is still under attack. Cerberus is assaulting Grissom Academy to abduct its students, most of whom build Alliance tech or train as military biotics.
evidence.for_key: Grissom students assigned to Alliance support lines

evidence.text: During the war with the Reapers, Kahlee sends out a communication to have her students evacuated from the Academy before it is overrun by the Reapers. Initially, a turian cruiser responds, but after Samantha Traynor aboard the Normandy SR\-2 under Commander Shepard examines the signal, she finds that it is a fake and that it has the same false signatures that led Shepard into a Collector Ambush the previous year. Traynor says that it is in fact a Cerberus Cruiser heading for the Academy. Should Shepard choose to act on Traynor's information, upon arriving at the Academy, the Normandy finds the cruiser and a dozen fighters blockading the Academy. Kahlee contacts the Normandy and tells them that Cerberus has taken over the docking bays but she can get a cargo hatch open so Shepard's team can board to save her and her students. Joker pulls the Cruiser and fighters out of position and allows Cortez flying one of the Normandy's Kodiaks, and the squad to enter the Academy. After entering the Academy and eliminating the Cerberus troops in the hall, Shepard manages to reach the room she has taken shelter in and after forcing the door open, the Commander tells Kahlee it's safe to leave her cover. Kahlee begins working on a computer in an attempt to locate any remaining students in the Academy while filling in Shepard on their latest efforts to create a Biotic Strike Team composed of their most talented students. Throughout the remainder of the mission, she aids Shepard via comm messages with directions for how to escape the station, eventually finding a way to commandeer two Cerberus shuttles while Shepard is busy shepherding the kids. At the mission's conclusion, she thanks Shepard for the help. Kahlee also voices her opinion that the students, having proved themselves in their recent combat, may be ready to take on more than simple support roles. If Jack is the biotic instructor and Shepard assigns the students to biotic artillery strike teams on the front lines, Kahlee thinks the students are ready for such a role. Otherwise, she vehemently opposes the decision, saying that the students are not up to the task without an instructor. When Shepard mentions Anderson, Kahlee expresses a sense of deep caring and concern for the Admiral and his safety. Later, Shepard can read a message Kahlee sends to Anderson from Liara's terminal, stating that he better stay alive and stay safe, for her sake. Kahlee makes her contribution to the war effort after the Grissom Academy incident, marshaling and coordinating personnel and resources she has at her disposal. If Jack is alive, Kahlee periodically checks in with her and the kids. If Jack is alive, the Grissom survivors were relegated to support duties, and Shepard chooses to use the Crucible at the battle for Earth, Kahlee resumes her old duties at the Alliance, standing alongside Jack and their students from the academy. If Shepard does not go to Grissom Academy in time, Anderson will inform Shepard that the Academy was overrun by Cerberus. He mentions Kahlee during the conversation and presumes she was killed in the attack.

evidence.text: In 2186 during the Reaper invasion, though war would close most schools, fewer than twenty teachers and students stayed at Grissom Academy to train biotics and prototype technology for the Alliance. Unfortunately, the Academy is attacked by Cerberus forces seeking to capture the students. The attack goes unnoticed because Cerberus uses a turian military signal to broadcast that the station is being evacuated by turian ships. Specialist Traynor and EDI connect the signal to a similar one known to have been used by the Illusive Man to lure Commander Shepard to a Collector Cruiser. If the Commander decides to travel there, upon arrival Jeff "Joker" Moreau uses the Normandy SR\-2 to distract the Cerberus cruiser and fighters guarding the station while Shepard and the team board it. Shepard encounters Kahlee Sanders, who has barricaded herself in a security room, and goes on to rescue the station's remaining students. After the students are evacuated, Grissom Academy is abandoned. The Academy and nearby Elysium later fall to the Reapers. If Shepard decides against going to the academy, the Cerberus kidnapping operation succeeds and the victims are subverted into working for the organization, like Jack if she survived the suicide mission.

evidence.text: **Military Strength:** 100 The old saying "every marine is a rifleman" still holds true in the Alliance. Every marine enlistee, from clerk to sniper, goes through a period of infantry training. As a result, the 103rd Marine Division is Earth's largest collection of Special Forces soldiers. Officers from notable battles, such as the Skyllian Blitz and the First Contact War, run harsh training exercises in a variety of environments, insisting the marines be prepared to storm any beach, on any planet. This training has been useful in the Reaper War, as the 103rd can be fighting in the arctic desert one week, crawling through jungles the next. evidence.text:
Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation was a Mass Effect 3 mission acquired after Priority: Palaven, when Samantha Traynor and EDI determined that a turian rescue signal answering an Academy evac request was actually a Cerberus fake and the station was still in danger. Cerberus forces were attacking Grissom Academy in the Petra Nebula to kidnap its students, most of whom were producing Alliance tech or training as military biotics. The mission had to be completed before Priority: The Citadel II or it was permanently failed.

With too many Cerberus ships to fight, Joker created a diversion so Shepard's shuttle could enter a cargo hold opened by Kahlee Sanders, who went back with Anderson to his Spectre-candidate days. Shepard freed Sanders from the security office, then fought through corridors and rooms rescuing scattered students, including Reiley Bellarmine and his dying sister Seanne. In Orion Hall, biotic students held off Assault Troopers and an Atlas; if a Mass Effect 2 save was imported and Jack survived the Suicide Mission, Jack led them and punched Shepard in the face on arrival (followed by a kiss if they had romanced). Otherwise Ensign Jason Prangley took charge. The squad then fought heavy waves of Centurions, Guardians, Combat Engineers, and Atlas mechs through two halves of the Atrium and a docking area, aided by empty Atlas mechs and by tech students including Octavia, with David Archer vouching for Shepard if Overlord was completed on the Paragon route.

During the final escape the wounded Rodriguez fell behind; whoever led the biotics smashed the glass to save her. If Jack led, everyone survived; if Prangley led, he was shot and killed. Afterward Shepard chose to assign the students as support (rolled into the Alliance 103rd Marine Division, +50 war assets, Paragon) or as a frontline Biotic Company (+75 war assets, Renegade), a choice that also set Jack's epilogue slide. Rewards included 25,000 credits, weapon mods, the Mnemonic Visor, and the Serrice Council Chestplate. If the mission expired, Jack was captured, turned into a Phantom, and had to be killed at Cerberus Headquarters, and Gavin Archer could commit suicide during Arrae: Ex-Cerberus Scientists.

evidence.section: Grissom Academy and the student squad (Mass Effect 3)
evidence.text: Shepard finds Jack leading a squad of biotic students at Grissom Academy during the Reaper War. She had "some free time" after Mass Effect 2; the Alliance brass knew she had helped Shepard and offered her the teaching post, and the students "responded well to her teaching style." She calls herself "The Psychotic Biotic." Her students include Rodriguez, whom she rides hard: "I will destroy you." — "You couldn't destroy wet tissue paper. Drink your juice, Rodriguez." Getting the students out alive, Jack promises them tattoos — "my treat" — an Ascension Project logo, a glowing fist, "maybe a unicorn for Rodriguez." Afterward there is an argument about how the students should be deployed. Jack and the students trained for barrier work to protect frontline squads; the Alliance wants to use them as another artillery unit. Shepard say they will be deployed as supports, as per Jack's recommendation to protect them. Once the students are formally military, the crew needle her: will she wear a uniform, or "just get the officer bars tattooed on"? Joker jokes about a swear jar — "I bet if we empty that thing we can afford another cruiser" — because Jack "promised to watch her language to maintain the necessary professionalism." Jack tells Shepard that the "little shits are useless without me, so I've got to stick with them — I'm dependable now, apparently. I blame you for this." She credits Shepard's "little suicide squad" with teaching her something about teamwork.
evidence.for_key: Grissom students assigned to Alliance support lines

evidence.text:
Ensign Jason Prangley was a biotic student at Jon Grissom Academy. He arrived at Grissom at age six, a shy child who barely spoke, and was known for constantly reading and studying battles, with some peers calling him a brownnoser. He proved capable of leadership when circumstances demanded it.

During the 2186 Reaper invasion, Cerberus attacked Grissom Academy to forcibly conscript its gifted students. If Jack survived the Suicide Mission, Prangley was among the students she protected; he was nearly killed by Atlas fire before his teacher intervened. When Commander Shepard arrived, Jason aided the firefight, providing biotic support strikes so that he and his teacher could retreat to higher ground. Afterward Jack derided his biotic fields as "weak," and he noticeably improved in later battles.

If Jack did not survive the Suicide Mission, Prangley interacted with Shepard in her place during the evacuation. Shepard found him stepping up to save Ensign Rodriguez from Atlas fire. Jason reported that their commanding officer had been killed, leaving him assuming command, and spoke on the students' behalf that they needed time to recharge after the strenuous exertion of biotics. In this scenario, Prangley later died protecting Rodriguez again from Cerberus troops just short of the hijacked escape shuttles. The survivors eulogized him aboard the shuttles, and Shepard invoked his memory to motivate the other students, either channeling their anger at his loss or holding up his sacrifice as an example to follow. Datapads left by Cerberus troops around the Academy indicate Prangley was specifically targeted as a prized acquisition.
evidence.for_key: Grissom students assigned to Alliance support lines

evidence.text:
The Ascension Project was a renewed human biotics training program that succeeded BAaT. It focused on the children of the victims of three element zero "accidents" that occurred across the Systems Alliance in 2170 on four separate colonies, including Yandoa; although the industrial accidents happened under suspicious circumstances, no link between them was ever found. On Yandoa alone, thirty-seven children were born with biotic abilities and were all sent to the Ascension Project. Established around 2176, the Project was based at the Jon Grissom Academy, a medium-sized space station orbiting the human colony of Elysium in the Skyllian Verge.

Unlike BAaT, the Project was not a military-exclusive venture; it invited civilian support and welcomed visits and input from attendees' families. It had three main aims: to develop and monitor new L4 implants (biotic amplifiers with built-in VI interfaces for monitoring implanted subjects); to help biotics maximize their field potential; and to help biotics integrate into human society. The last aim held an important curriculum place, with students given philosophical and moral guidance on the responsibilities of using biotics. Staff were nonetheless equipped with Aldrin Labs stun guns to subdue students who misused their abilities, though these were used on a student only once.

At some point the Project was infiltrated by Cerberus operatives seeking research on human biotics in order to "save" humanity. Cerberus left Dr. Jiro Toshiwa to monitor events there, particularly to study Gillian Grayson's progress. Known students included Gillian Grayson, Nick, and Seshaun; known staff included Dr. Kahlee Sanders, Security Chief Hendel Mitra, Dr. Jiro Toshiwa, Dr. Sanchez, and maths professor Jacob Berg. During the Grissom Academy evacuation in Mass Effect 3, Samantha Traynor told Shepard about the program; if Shepard was a Vanguard, Sentinel, or Adept, she said Shepard would have joined it had it existed during the Commander's youth.
evidence.for_key: Grissom students assigned to Alliance support lines

evidence.text:
The Jon Grissom Academy was a Systems Alliance space station commissioned in 2176, in orbit over the human colony of Elysium in the Petra Nebula. Its stated mission was to serve human students with excellence and passion for math, science, and the liberal arts, with an entirely human student body ranging from early teens to mid-twenties. Its population was 8,620; the station was 1.1 km long and weighed 375,000 metric tons. Though not heavily advertised, it also offered classes for biotic students through its main program, the Ascension Project, which trained and monitored young biotics and helped them integrate into society after graduation. Unlike the earlier military program BAaT (Biotic Acclimation and Temperance Training), its training was not exclusively military. The Academy also employed scientific personnel, including Dr. Kahlee Sanders, to develop synthetic intelligence systems and biotic amplifiers such as the L4 implants.

In 2183 the Ascension Project was its most prominent program. In Mass Effect 2, Shepard could send David Archer to the Academy after his brother Dr. Gavin Archer used him in an experiment to control the geth. After Jon Grissom's death, a memorial plaque was erected in the mess hall; six months later, the Reaper-controlled Paul Grayson boarded the station seeking information on the Ascension Project, disabling or killing most of the personnel before David Anderson, Kahlee Sanders, and Kai Leng arrived and killed him.

In 2186 during the Reaper invasion, fewer than twenty teachers and students remained to train biotics and prototype technology for the Alliance. Cerberus attacked to capture the students, masking the assault by broadcasting a turian military signal claiming the station was being evacuated by turian ships; Traynor and EDI linked the signal to one the Illusive Man had used to lure Shepard to a Collector Cruiser. If Shepard traveled there, Joker used the Normandy SR-2 to distract the Cerberus cruiser while the team boarded, found Kahlee Sanders barricaded in a security room, and rescued the remaining students, who were evacuated before the Academy was abandoned. The Academy and Elysium later fell to the Reapers. If Shepard did not go, the kidnapping succeeded and the victims, including Jack if she survived the suicide mission, were subverted into working for Cerberus.
evidence.for_key: Grissom students assigned to Alliance support lines

evidence.text: - **Availability:** Very early \| **First Playable:** Prologue: Awakening - **Specialty:** Biotics, Combat support - **Weapons:** Shotguns, Heavy Pistols **Powers** | | **Barrier:** 250 / **Health:** 200 | | | --- | --- | | **Class: Cerberus Operative** | | | Pull | **Starts at rank 1** | | Incendiary Ammo | **Starts at rank 1** | | Cerberus Operative |  | | Barrier | **Unlocked when Jacob is loyal.** | |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | **Note:** Jacob Taylor and Miranda Lawson can each have 31 points maximum available for distribution, not the 30 that is usual for squadmates. **Overview** Jacob has a very similar kit to Jack, wielding a shotgun, an ammo power, and Pull, though his class and loyalty powers are geared more towards defense than offense. Pull once maxed is easily the strongest disabling power in the game, able to render multiple enemies instantly helpless and vulnerable to weapons fire or combos with Warp, and for a long duration. Jacob's ammo power is Incendiary Ammo, the most versatile of the ammo powers: not only does it deal good damage to most organic health and all forms of armor, it stops the health regeneration of enemies like krogan and vorcha, and panics most organic humanoid targets. Unlocking Jacob's Barrier can create the conundrum that he will constantly reactivate it during battles even if Squad Power Use is disabled, making it much harder to call upon his Pull. The only way to have a loyal Jacob but avoid this problem is to reset his powers using the Advanced Training terminal at the Shadow Broker's Base (requires either Lair of the Shadow Broker DLC or **Legendary Edition**) and invest no points in Barrier; this also applies to Grunt's Fortification and Legion's Geth Shield Boost.

evidence.text: Ammo powers return in Mass Effect 3 and in single\-player work much the same way as they did in Mass Effect 2\. However, one improvement in Mass Effect 3 is that ammo powers no longer have a recharge time and can still be activated even when other powers are on cooldown. In addition, cryo, tech, and fire ammo effects can set up corresponding Power Combos on affected targets. In single\-player, evolutions of ammo powers that share the power with party members still exist, but the ammo power will work at reduced effectiveness for all but the owner of the power, dealing less damage and triggering secondary effects less readily. For ease of assigning a particular ammo power to specific weapons and/or party members, Shepard should carry at least two weapons, even if one is only a lightweight placeholder. Ammo power assignments on weapons for the entire squad are remembered by game saves. There is almost no way to deactivate ammo powers entirely from weapons once they are activated, except for loading a save from before any ammo powers were turned on. Finding a new gun and selecting "Change Loadout" or accessing a weapon bench during a mission will deactivate all ammo powers across the entire squad. The following squadmates available during story missions have access to ammo powers of their own: Ashley Williams, James Vega, Garrus Vakarian, and Liara T'Soni. Squad members will automatically activate their own ammo powers in combat for their personal use, even if Squad Power Use is turned off in the menus; for the party\-sharing evolutions to apply, however, a squadmate must be explicitly ordered to activate their ammo power by the player. Shepard can have access to ammo powers either as class powers or as bonus powers. The ammo powers available in single\-player Mass Effect 3 are: - Armor\-Piercing Ammo - Cryo Ammo - Disruptor Ammo - Incendiary Ammo - Warp Ammo Ammo powers deal their own unique damage type as a percentage of the "base" damage of the weapon they are augmenting, which is then added on to that base damage. Every ammo power except Cryo Ammo has its own unique multipliers against certain enemy protection types that improves its added "ammo damage". Ammo power damage can be further boosted by a few other modifiers, but it is worth noting that the various evolutions of the above ammo powers that improve headshot damage do **not** improve added ammo damage; instead, these evolutions work as a multiplicative enhancement of base weapon damage when scoring headshots. The above ammo powers do not exist in multiplayer mode, but single\-use ammo bonuses can provide many of the same effects, as well as a few more unique to multiplayer.

evidence.text:
This gameplay guide summarizes the combat abilities, strengths, and weaknesses of the squadmates Commander Shepard can recruit in Mass Effect 2, listed roughly in order of availability. In Legendary Edition all former DLC characters are unlocked, though mission-exclusive members remain limited to their missions.

Jacob Taylor combines a shotgun, Incendiary Ammo, and a maxed Pull, the strongest disabling power in the game, though his loyalty Barrier auto-reactivates and interferes with casting Pull. Miranda Lawson is defined by versatility: Overload, Warp, the mid-game Slam for a disable, and the powerful party-wide Cerberus Officer passive; she and Jacob each get 31 power points instead of the usual 30. Kasumi Goto offers Overload plus the unique high-damage Shadow Strike and a wide-radius Flashbang Grenade that hinders even protected enemies. Zaeed Massani is a long-range specialist and the only non-Infiltrator/Soldier with Disruptor Ammo, plus crowd-control Concussive Shot and Inferno Grenade. Garrus Vakarian again pairs weapon proficiency with Overload and gains Armor-Piercing Ammo, making him the only squadmate with both a shield-killing power and an ammo power. Grunt is a near-unkillable close-combat juggernaut with regenerating krogan health, Krogan Vitality upgrades, Fortification, the Claymore shotgun, and Incendiary Ammo.

Jack specializes in biotic crowd control with Pull and Shockwave, and her Warp Ammo is the only ammo power that damages barriers. Mordin Solus has only tech powers, no anti-shield or anti-barrier option, but excels against armor with Incineration Blast and disables groups with Full Cryo Blast. Samara and Morinth are near-identical biotic powerhouses differing only in loyalty power: Samara's Area Reave counters mass barriers, while Morinth's Dominate works like AI Hacking on organics. Tali'Zorah vas Neema is situational until Energy Drain, strong against synthetics, with long-lasting AI Hacking. Thane Krios can build as a pure sniper with Shredder Ammo or as a biotic with Warp. Legion is the only squadmate able to wield the M-98 Widow and can reach the highest weapon damage in the game, but has no defense-stripping power. Liara T'Soni rejoins temporarily during Lair of the Shadow Broker with Singularity, Warp, and a Stasis that stops even protected enemies. The page closes with weapon, power, and outfit reference tables.

evidence.text: - In Mass Effect 3, contrary to its in\-game description, Incinerate does not halt enemy health regeneration. evidence.text:
The Praetorian was a slow-moving aerial Collector construct assembled from thirty deformed husks fused together, armed with twin particle beams and protected by an armored carapace and a strong biotic barrier. It was likely named after the Praetorian Guard of the Roman Emperors.

In 2185 Commander Shepard fought Praetorians during Mass Effect 2, once at the end of the Horizon mission and once during the escape from the Collector Cruiser; several also attacked the Normandy SR-2. In that game the Praetorian attacked with a roughly three-second particle beam and with "Death Choir," a ground strike followed by a near-instant-kill area blast that also fully recharged its barrier. It was invulnerable during Death Choir, which it used after every quarter of its armor was stripped by weapons fire (but not by armor-damaging powers such as Incinerate, Warp, or Reave). It was immune to Stasis, Charge, and Dominate. Recommended tactics included armor-piercing or Warp Ammo, the M-9 Tempest or Geth Plasma Shotgun against its barrier, keeping distance and moving perpendicular to its beams, and circling large cover it would not fly over.

In the animated film Paragon Lost, the Collectors deployed a Praetorian on Fehl Prime during the colonist abductions, built in part from Delta Squad marine Kamille; its attacks and barrier glowed green rather than blue, and it was destroyed by James Vega after the ship Essex disabled its barrier.

Praetorians returned in Mass Effect 3 multiplayer with the Retaliation Pack and in the Armax Arsenal Arena combat simulator. There they swept their twin particle cannons in a wide line that penetrated thin cover and dealt continuous heavy damage (the most damaging enemy ranged attack in the game), used a long-range pounce, and could grab enemies for an instant kill. They were highly mobile despite their size, had very high armor and a sizeable barrier, put up a spherical barrier that blocked most power damage when hit while hovering, and could themselves be "possessed" for extra durability. They often appeared in groups of two.
evidence.for_key: barrier work and ammo modding in the Alliance 103rd

evidence.text:
Warp Ammo was an ammo power in Mass Effect 2 and the single-player mode of Mass Effect 3, described as transforming absorbed biotic energy into heavier weapon damage against health, armor, and biotic barriers. It was distinct from the Warp Rounds ammo bonus in Mass Effect 3 multiplayer.

In Mass Effect 2, a biotic mass effect field keyed into the ammo increased its damage against health, armor, and barriers and did extra health damage to targets affected by biotics. Ranks 1-3 raised the bonus from 15% to 35% of weapon damage; rank 4 evolved it into Heavy Warp Ammo (50% of weapon damage, likened to a miniature disruptor torpedo) or Squad Warp Ammo (35%, shared with the whole squad). The bonus damage was doubled against enemies lifted by Pull, Singularity, or Slam, but gave no extra damage against non-physics powers such as Reave or Dominate or against targets merely knocked down. It was the only Mass Effect 2 ammo power that dealt bonus damage to barriers, making it the best choice for sniping barrier-protected enemies. It was available to Shepard via Advanced Training and to Jack as a loyalty power.

In Mass Effect 3, Warp Ammo could confer up to three benefits: boosted damage against health, armor, and barriers; a large bonus against enemies primed for Biotic Explosions; and armor weakening that reduced armored enemies' damage mitigation by 25% (50% with the rank 6 Enhanced Warp evolution). Rank 1 gave +15% health and armor damage, +30% barrier damage, -25% armor weakening, and +50% damage to lifted targets. Rank 2 was Biotic Combo, rank 3 Damage, rank 4 Damage or Squad Bonus (squadmates at 50% effectiveness), rank 5 Ammo Capacity or Headshots, and rank 6 Damage or Enhanced Warp. Warp Ammo dealt 2x damage to barriers inherently. Since Patch 1.04, the lifted-target bonus applied to all enemies primed for biotic combos, including those under Warp, Reave, Dark Channel, or Stasis, but not to shields. The armor-weakening debuff was party-friendly and lasted about two seconds. It was the only ammo power effective against both barriers and armor, making it efficient against Banshees, Adjutants, and Praetorians. Single-player users were Liara T'Soni, Jack, and Shepard as a bonus power; it did not exist in multiplayer.
evidence.for_key: barrier work and ammo modding in the Alliance 103rd

evidence.text:
The Phantom was a Cerberus combat unit encountered in Mass Effect 3, described as the result of reverse-engineered Reaper technology: agile biotic cyborgs specializing in evasive maneuvers and firing from cover. Their implants remained a mystery to the Alliance, but they were known to project personal biotic barriers. They fought at close quarters with monomolecular blades, a single stab from which could kill instantly, and carried a semi-automatic kinetic projectile weapon built into the right gauntlet. They could briefly cloak to regenerate health and recharge barriers, so the Alliance recommended personal confirmation of a Phantom's death.

Defensively, Phantoms relied on agility, sidestepping, rolling and leaping away from fire, and used suit-mounted stabilizing thrusters to recover quickly from knockdown. They could raise a localized biotic barrier making them briefly immune to most powers, and were always immune to long-duration shock-stun effects (Disruptor Ammo, Overload, Energy Drain, Sabotage), could not be fully frozen by cryo powers, did not panic when on fire, and were immune to grab instant-kills. A Phantom's barrier was roughly twice as strong as its health.

Notable tactically for being no larger than basic infantry despite "super elite" status, Phantoms were best engaged from a distance. Their gauntlet blaster could strip 875 shield points in a single shot on Gold. Their sword could be broken by accurate hitscan or explosive-round fire, after which the Phantom would hang back in cover and fire its palm weapon instead. Their self-healing could be blocked by Reave and permanently prevented by Incendiary Ammo damage. Stasis or Submission Net left them helpless for headshots, and they often paired with a Nemesis, which acted as bait. An advancing Phantom emitted a low electronic muttering, but a stationary one was silent and could ambush the unwary.

evidence.text:
A collection of Jack dialogue and party-banter clips spanning Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3: a cut Mass Effect 2 conversation about red sand, the Mass Effect 3 scene introducing her varren Eezo, Normandy confrontations with Miranda, her time as an instructor at Grissom Academy leading a biotic student squad, a reunion with Garrus, and the Citadel DLC reconciliation with Miranda. It is useful as voice reference and for Jack's personal continuity. Representative lines:

- Jack, in the cut red sand conversation, when Shepard notes she takes drugs herself: "If I don't, I wake up screaming, with furniture slamming into the wall."
- Jack, on why an asari would use red sand despite already being biotic: "You get a great high, too."
- Jack, introducing her naturally biotic varren from Thessia: "Who's my badass biotic? Who's my badass biotic?"
- Jack, agreeing to hold off her fight with Miranda for the mission: "Sure, I'll do my part. I'd hate to see her die before I get a chance to fillet her myself."
- Jack, when Shepard keeps visiting to ask questions in Mass Effect 2: "You don't need to know someone to sleep with them. You just have to know where to put it."
- Jack, riding her Grissom Academy student: "You couldn't destroy wet tissue paper. Drink your juice, Rodriguez."
- Jack, on staying with her students in Mass Effect 3: "The little shits are useless without me, so I've got to stick with them — I'm dependable now, apparently. I blame you for this."
- Jack, reuniting with Garrus: "As charming as ever. Good to see you again, Garrus." — Garrus: "You still look like [expletive]."
- Jack, in the Citadel DLC after Miranda concedes Cerberus was wrong about her: "Wow. Thanks. I still really hate you, but you have fantastic tits." — Miranda: "All right, I can live with that."
- Jack, to Shepard at the Citadel party: "The duty rosters can wait. Right now you're on shore leave, Shepard." And: "Everybody knows you can't dance."

Kelly Chambers' observation is also quoted: "She pushes people away yet approaches sex casually… If you want her respect, think twice." Miranda, during the sub-deck confrontation, insists "it wasn't Cerberus, not really" and that Jack "was clearly a mistake."

Reading the first email is optional, while reading the second email activates the mission in the Journal. **Omega: Come see me** --- From: Aria T'Loak Subject: Come see me Shepard, I have something important to discuss with you. It's sensitive, so we'll need privacy. I'll arrange for that soon. In the meantime, come see me on the Citadel in the aptly named Purgatory. I have a few ideas for your war. **Omega: It's time** --- From: Aria T'Loak Subject: It's time Shepard, I'm ready to discuss that pet project I mentioned when we spoke in Purgatory. evidence.text: “I'm dependable now. I blame you for this, Shepard.” In 2186, provided she survived the Suicide Mission, Jack has altered her appearance, having grown out her hair into a pony tail, but retaining the shaven sides. She now sports a punky studded jacket over a white top that reveals her midriff and its numerous tattoos. She has become more mature, and states that some of Shepard's attitude rubbed off on her. Sometime after the Collectors' defeat, Jack was approached by the Systems Alliance and offered a teaching position at the Grissom Academy to train biotics for combat. She accepted and agreed to tone down her profanity to maintain the level of professionalism expected from teachers. Her students apparently responded well to her unconventional teaching style, mimicking her trash talk ("I will destroy you!") and sticking affectionate appellations like "the psychotic biotic". Jack herself grew attached to her charges in return, considering them the family she never had, and promises to exact retribution against anyone who screws with her kids. Jack is present on the station during Cerberus' attempt to kidnap gifted students for their cause, defending hers from being captured. Shepard finds Jack in the middle of shielding one of her students from incoming Atlas fire, and while Shepard's team takes care of the opposition Jack rallies to her kids on higher ground, helping project a biotic barrier and supporting biotic strikes. Jack's fist lands on Shepard's face the moment the smoke clears, the exact reason why depends on Shepard's previous actions. If a male Shepard romanced her, she hit him for leaving her, then immediately kisses him passionately afterwards. If Shepard expresses misgivings about previously working with Cerberus, Jack cites either handing over the Collector Base to them or the deaths they've caused as her reason. If Shepard merely reminds her how they saved her ass, Jack sarcastically asks if they want a medal. Whichever the case, Shepard's squadmates interject and Jack has some choice replies for some of them. After giving instructions to her students and admonishments to Jason Prangley, Jack relates to Shepard the things she's been up to over the past few months. If the conversation turns into improving the students' endurance and conditioning, Jack specifically recalls her time in the Suicide Mission either throwing husks around or being Shepard's biotic bubble specialist whenever the students complain, telling the kids she kept thinking that she should've let Mordin handle her job instead as he can "talk \[the Collectors] to death." If Mordin died, though, Jack feels bad, recalling the "wicked sex advice" he often gave. Once all the catch\-up is over she stays put until Shepard paves the way for their exit route. One of her students, Ensign Rodriguez, wavers when Cerberus starts messaging the students, and Jack gives the student a dressing\-down. Jack either gives Rodriguez her coarse affirmation of her student's abilities, or shoves the surgery scars inflicted during her Cerberus captivity into her scared student's view, angrily asserting that surrender is tantamount to being meat on a slab. The Ensign sets her head straight after this, and Jack leads the students in shadowing Shepard's team from higher ground while the squad clears out the bulk of Cerberus resistance. Privately, Jack believes her kids aren't yet ready for the realities of war, but Shepard can influence her into letting the students run loose for a while even if they're only fighting from relatively safe positions. Jack, Shepard and Kahlee Sanders eventually manage to help the students escape. Jack, in a good mood, wants to treat her kids to tattoos at the next place they dock. If a male Shepard chose to break with her earlier, Jack even mentions hanging on to the N7 tattoo on her ass she previously planned to burn off. As they make their way back to the Normandy, Jack decides to break her self\-censoring when Joker takes note of the fact and wisecracks that if Jack had a swear jar the cash inside would've been sufficient to buy a cruiser. After the rescue from Jon Grissom Academy, Jack can be found on the Citadel in Purgatory Bar after the attempted Cerberus coup reading duty rosters for her kids even while on shore leave. Shepard can either tell her to keep at it, or convince her to lighten up a bit, which colors Jack's responses throughout the conversation. If Shepard thinks Jack fits in snugly to military life, Jack says that their little suicide squad apparently taught her something about teamwork. If the students had been sent to the front lines, Jack mentions her kids are being sent into hot spots for hit\-and\-runs and she's making sure the higher\-ups won't give them something way out of their league.
evidence.for_key: Jack as instructor at the Purgatory reading duty rosters

evidence.text: The Blue Suns also own the maximum security prison Purgatory. The prison is run by Warden Kuril who claims that Purgatory is for "the good of the galactic community", despite the harsh methods used to maintain order, including carrying out torture, beatings and even murder (blowing prisoners out of airlocks as examples). Prisoners are also sold to vengeful victims/relatives or to groups with large enough finances, such as Cerberus. The Blue Suns have a substantial presence within the prison and have utilized several YMIR Mechs to act as heavy\-hitters in case a riot broke out. The prison is known to hold the most dangerous criminals in the galaxy. The Blue Suns agree to keep them imprisoned only if their home planets agree to continually pay for their incarceration. Failure to pay is grounds for releasing the inmate at an unknown time and place on their homeworld; considering inmates like Jack inhabit the prison, most worlds presumably pay. Shepard will travel to Purgatory to recruit Jack, who has been purchased by Cerberus from the Blue Suns. Early on, Warden Kuril betrays Shepard, attempting to imprison the Commander, who he states is more valuable as a prisoner than a customer, leading to a fight breaking out between Shepard's team and Kuril's Blue Suns, with Shepard eventually releasing the entire cell block in order to free Jack from cryo containment. This causes a full\-scale riot throughout the ship, with the Blue Suns attempting to restore control, kill Shepard and re\-capture Jack. They ultimately fail with Shepard killing Kuril and Jack joining the Commander’s crew. Cerberus then retracts the funds they paid. A news report reveals that the Purgatory was destroyed, with the Blue Suns losing yet another piece of influence.

evidence.text:
Citadel: Aria T'Loak was the preamble mission for the Mass Effect 3: Omega DLC, requiring that DLC and completion of Priority: Palaven. Aria T'Loak sent Shepard two emails: the first, received after the primarch's retrieval from Menae, indicated the DLC was installed and invited Shepard to meet her at the Purgatory bar on the Citadel; the second, sent after Shepard had spoken with her at Purgatory at least once, told Shepard to come to Dock 42, where a batarian named Bray would be waiting. Reading the second email activated the mission in the Journal.

At Dock 42 Shepard met Bray, one of Aria's batarian guards, and boarded a skycar with Aria for a joyride around the Presidium, kept private because of the sensitive nature of the plan. Aria explained her intention to retake Omega from Cerberus: she had assembled a fleet to break through the Cerberus ships guarding the station, but expected the real fighting to happen on foot through the station. She named the leader of the occupation as Oleg Petrovsky, admitted she had little intelligence on enemy ground forces, but claimed to know exploitable secrets about Omega. She offered Shepard troops and supplies for the Reaper war in exchange for help retaking Omega, on the condition that Shepard come alone, without squadmates, while her forces engaged the bulk of the enemy elsewhere. No morality points were awarded. The skycar dropped Shepard and Bray at a docking bay; Aria left her fleet's coordinates with Bray, urged secrecy while on the Citadel, and Shepard was automatically returned to the Normandy SR-2. The mission was written by Neil Pollner.

evidence.text:
A catalogue of dialogue unique to Jack when she is in Shepard's squad in Mass Effect 2, organized into location-triggered lines, "talk to squad mate" conversations, and spontaneous combat and ambient barks. Notable in the collection: on the Citadel, Jack tells a story in the bar bathroom of being sexually assaulted in the Purgatory prison showers and then hunting down and murdering every one of her attackers. Representative verbatim lines:

- Jack, meeting Legion at the end of the Reaper IFF mission, on whether to take the geth: she favors taking it "so it can be carved into a lamp."
- Jack, on Legion's loyalty mission, objecting to rewriting the heretics: "If you screw with my head, made me nod and smile at everything... I'd rather you blew my head off. Let me die as me."
- Jack, dying if chosen to lead the second diversion squad in the Suicide Mission: "Too many... tore me up. How'd you talk me into this? Heh... I wasn't supposed to care." (Romanced male Shepard: "Too many of them... I knew I'd get hit on this job. I was too happy... too happy with you.")
- Jack, when Miranda is suggested to lead the second squad: "No one wants to take orders from you."
- Jack, on Horizon after the first Collector encounter: "Peaceful. Usually takes a lot of chemicals for me to get this kind of quiet."
- Jack, landing on Korlus and hearing Jedore's PA orders: "I already want to kill this person." Later: "Can we shut that bitch up, already?"

Other tagged lines include her approving of Shepard throwing a merc through a window during Thane's recruitment ("I could take notes from you, Shepard"), betting 15 credits that Niftu Cal will die, and calling the Shadow Broker's remark that her corpse is valuable during Lair of the Shadow Broker.

evidence.page: Getting the Biotic Students Off Grissom Academy
evidence.text: Getting the Biotic Students Off Grissom Academy. 2186, after Priority: Palaven, before Priority: The Citadel II Jon Grissom Academy, Petra Nebula — security office, classrooms, Orion Hall, the Atrium, the docking area; then the Normandy Shepard fights through classrooms and corridors while a Cerberus commander tells students over the intercom they will be safe if they do not resist and operatives drag students off. Shepard rescues scattered students, among them Reiley Bellarmine and his badly wounded sister Seanne.
evidence.for_key: Jack's students under fire on Palaven

evidence.text: Dr. Angersol frantically comms for backup when the doors to his office are demolished by sheer biotic power. Jack steps inside and executes the doctor, a figure from her Subject Zero past. The Illusive Man appears before her via hologram, attempting to reason with her, but Jack would hear none of it. At a remote Cerberus outpost elsewhere, Kai Leng hooks in Rasa for a mission. A Cerberus training facility is under attack, and the Illusive Man dispatches them both to retrieve the perpetrator, Jack: dead or alive, through whatever means necessary. Leng and Rasa arrive at the training facility a short time later, finding huge swathes of destruction in Subject Zero's wake. The presence of multiple people out to get the target makes Rasa think about Jack's possible origins and the threat she poses. Leng simply suggests they should find her before the others \- the Blue Suns mercenaries \- do. With the facility in lockdown, Jack makes her way to its main reactor. She comes across a bald man claiming to be a biotic trainee of the facility. The man doesn't know where the reactor is, but he takes her to his fellow students when she orders him to. The man claims to have had a better life under Cerberus tutelage, but Jack's own experiences with the organization tells her otherwise. On finding the other students she gives them a chance to learn the truth behind Cerberus by escaping with her, or stay and keep hoping that Cerberus is as benevolent as it seems to be. A good number of the students follow Jack as they try to make it out of the facility. A trio of Blue Suns mercs block their way, so Jack orders the students to sneak across while she presents herself as a diversion. Rasa and Leng arrive behind Jack when she's done bringing down the ceiling on the mercs. Brandishing his sword, Leng gives her one chance to surrender. Jack responds by unleashing a powerful biotic blast on the Cerberus operatives. She warns Rasa to stay down, but Leng is actually coming down on her from above. She senses it and biotically blasts the assassin again, this time hurling him higher up. More Blue Suns arrive at the scene and open fire on Jack, forcing her to throw up a biotic shield. She sees the students she's with securely behind Blue Suns lines. Enraged at the turn of events she starts making everything in the vicinity fly. Unfortunately, a krogan merc sneaks up from behind and docks her at the head, knocking her unconscious. The merc picks her up and hauls her away, to the Cerberus agents' consternation. The Illusive Man can still have Subject Zero, but the krogan wants triple the usual pay for all the losses he has incurred. As Leng and the students recover from the turn of events he chalks up the post\-mortem as a "colossal waste of time", but Rasa begs to differ: at the very least, the Illusive Man will now know what Jack is capable of.

evidence.text: Ben signed up to fight turians after his brother was killed during the aliens' bombardment of Shanxi's settlements. A master of munitions, he was a perfect recruit for Jack's prohumanity movement. Eventually he, Jack, and Eva formed a mercenary trio conducting guerrilla warfare under the employ of General Williams, and he served as Jack's right\-hand man.

evidence.text: As you approach the door, Kahlee will tell you that she has just received an emergency message from the students in Orion Hall. Before entering, take out the generator to the right of the door, which will allow Kahlee to address the students over the PA. She will inform them that help is here, and will warn the students not to let Cerberus take them alive. Proceed through the second door at the end of the corridor to see the biotic students defending themselves against Assault Troopers. If a Mass Effect 2 save was imported and Jack survived the Suicide Mission, she will be with the students; otherwise, Ensign Jason Prangley will step up and take charge. An Atlas breaks into the room. The students retreat behind a biotic barrier; you must defeat the enemies before the barrier wears down. The Atlas is dangerous if you get in its line of fire, but it is slow and will not take any more interest in Shepard than in your squadmates. The Assault Troopers and Centurions in the middle of the room are fast and may drift dangerously around your flanks, though they often get distracted attacking the students. **Tip:** On higher difficulty levels, you may want to concentrate on lowering the population of troopers before taking on the Atlas, particularly because it can regenerate its shields if left alone for a time. At the beginning of the encounter, the troopers will be huddled together, so using a few Power Combos can make quick work of them. Sabotage can force the Atlas to assist you temporarily if you have it available. After the battle, Jack punches Shepard in the face. If a male Shepard had a relationship with Jack in Mass Effect 2, the punch is followed up with a kiss, and the reason given for the punch is Shepard leaving her. Otherwise, the reason given is for previously trusting Cerberus. There will be opportunities for some unique interactions between Jack and several squad members, with an interesting variation if Garrus is present and also the love interest of a female Shepard. If Jack is not present, the students say that their CO was killed, leaving Prangley in charge. In addition, without the benefit of Jack as their teacher, a student, Ensign Rodriguez, will ask you if you ever forget the first time you kill someone, giving you extra Paragon or Renegade points. The students need a few minutes to rest and recharge after their ordeal fending off Cerberus. Cortez comes over the communications channel to say that the Cerberus cruiser is returning, and it's too dangerous for him to keep the shuttle docked for more than another two minutes. Shepard orders him to get back to the Normandy, then informs Kahlee, who comes up with an alternative way out of the facility. Relative to where you first entered the room, immediately turn left and find a data log (\+20 XP) listing Prangley as a high\-priority capture target, and the Cerberus camera control Kahlee tasks you with finding. On the opposite side of the room is a Med Kit. In the balcony room where the students are, you will find the Assault Rifle Precision Scope at the back of the room and a datapad (\+1875 Credits) at the front. Use the door override controls in the middle of the back wall to open the door to the Atrium. **Tip:** If this is a first playthrough it may be a good time to check if you have leveled up. Head back downstairs. You can speak to Jack for some exposition if she is present. If asked, she will express her opinion that the students are likely better off as support units rather than on the front lines. Her dialog here can vary depending on if she was the biotic specialist during the Suicide Mission, and also depending on the fate of Mordin Solus if this is after Priority: Tuchanka. Save here because you won't get to save after you open the door. When ready, proceed to the door to the Atrium, located at the end of the corridor under the balcony room. The biotics suggest that they follow a different route to the squad, attacking Cerberus from above. Respond however you like, then get treated to the Cerberus announcer telling the students that the Alliance soldiers are going to get them killed and that they should just surrender. Again, respond how you wish; Jack's response here will vary depending on your dialog choice.

evidence.text:
Ben Hislop was a human mercenary and munitions master who appeared in Mass Effect: Evolution. He signed up to fight turians after his brother was killed during the turian bombardment of Shanxi's settlements during the First Contact War, and fought in the resistance on occupied Shanxi. Recruited into Jack Harper's prohumanity movement, he formed a mercenary trio with Jack and Eva Coré, conducting guerrilla warfare under the employ of General Williams, and served as Jack's right-hand man.

On Shanxi, Ben's unit ambushed a turian patrol and he personally fought and captured the turian general Desolas Arterius with Jack's help. He wanted to execute Desolas but Jack kept the general alive for interrogation. On a mission to find the artifact Desolas sought, Ben antagonized him while Jack's scheme defeated the turian subordinates. Reaching the artifact inside a cave, Ben and Jack were ambushed by hooded figures revealed to be cyberized turians, which proved freakishly strong. When Ben touched the artifact to try to shut it off, he was electrocuted; Jack pried him free but was also affected, leaving both incapacitated. Desolas seized them and ordered Ben's body taken for study.

When Harper and Eva pursued Desolas to Illium, they found Ben alive but mutated into a synthetic form like the "meta-turians." He retained some sense of his identity but followed orders from Desolas and Saren, bringing the artifact, the Arca Monolith, to Palaven, where Desolas tried to replicate Harper's enhancement without creating mindless husks. The artifact commanded Ben to excavate a second artifact to accelerate the transformation. When Eva tried to haul Ben out and then to destroy the artifact, it commanded Ben to slam her head against a wall, killing her. Coming to his senses, a horrified Ben charged Desolas and rammed him into the artifact before he could shoot Harper; Saren tore Desolas away. Prolonged contact with the released energy instantly killed Ben, and his body was later vaporized when Saren ordered an orbital bombardment of the temple. Harper later included Ben's and Eva's names in his manifesto as he became the Illusive Man.

evidence.text:
Palaven was the turian homeworld, the third planet of the Trebia System in the Apien Crest cluster of the Milky Way. Alliance hero Jon Grissom, among the first humans to see it after the First Contact War, described its people as "made of steel". An asari diplomat had earlier called Palaven "a silver world of fortresses and fire". The planet's weak magnetic field left it poorly shielded from its sun, so most animal life developed metallic carapaces against solar radiation and photosynthetic life shut down vulnerable processes during daylight, repairing cellular damage at night. An Alliance travel advisory warned human visitors to wear enviro-suits or radiation protection.

The turians' martial attitude permeated every aspect of Palaven society, from architecture to art to politics, and its visibly fortified cities reflected this; after the turians joined the galactic community, internal conflicts became honor-bound affairs with few civilian casualties. Palaven was never occupied by an invading force until the Reapers, who brought overwhelming force, bombarded every city that resisted, and left the dust and smoke of pulverized cities as a breathing hazard across much of the planet, with water and power supplies nearly gone. The fight there nonetheless cost the Reapers dearly.

Shortly after the First Contact War, the mercenaries Jack Harper, Eva Coré, and the heavily modified Ben Hislop became the first three humans to set foot on Palaven, paraded through the streets by Desolas Arterius to persuade the populace to use the Arca Monolith. Garrus Vakarian grew up on Palaven and compared parts of it to Virmire. A Citadel business in Zakera Ward was named after the planet, and a regular shuttle route connected Palaven to Illium as of 2185. The Mass Effect 3 multiplayer map Firebase Condor was set on one of Palaven's moons.
